events.summary:
Through this evening, conditions will be favorable for waterspout
development over the offshore waters on the south side of the island
chain. Waterspouts will be most likely to form from showers and
thunderstorms that are nearly stationary. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Mariners are
encouraged to seek safe harbor immediately if a waterspout is
spotted.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 328 PM EDT, local law enforcement reported a number of road
closures in Isle of Palms, Mount Pleasant and surrounding areas from
ongoing flash flooding. Between 3 and 5.5 inches of rain have fallen
in these areas since around 1 pm. Emergency officials are describing
this situation as dangerous and are asking people to stay off the
roadways until conditions improve. The risk for additional flash
flooding has diminished, but it will take some time for conditions to
improve.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mount Pleasant, Isle Of Palms, Sullivan's Island, Mount Pleasant
Towne Centre, Boone Hall Plantation, Sullivans Island, Seaside
Farms, East Cooper Regional Medical Center and Snowden.

This includes I-526 between mile markers 29 and 31.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Urban and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
county, Palm Beach.

* WHEN...Until 530 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. Ponding of water in urban or other areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 326 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This will cause urban and small stream
flooding. Up to 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Boca Raton, Boynton Beach, Delray Beach, Highland Beach,
Ocean Ridge, Dunes Road, Village Of Golf, Kings Point, Gulf
Stream, Briny Breezes and Manalapan.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows are possible, flooding
caused by excessive rainfall over the Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar
is possible.

* WHERE...Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar in Ouray County Colorado,
including Dexter and Cutler Creek drainages and Highway 550... and
Cow Creek.

* WHEN...Until 515 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall is possible over the Gold Mountain
Burn Scar which could lead to flash flooding and/or debris flows,
particularly along highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter
Creek. Cow creek may also be affected. The debris flow can consist
of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 111 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Gold Mountain Burn Scar, including Cow Creek, and along
highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter Creek.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
